entities.summary: Lý Thái Tổ, personal name Lý Công Uẩn (李公蘊), was the founding emperor of the Lý dynasty. He reigned the empire for 18 years, from 1009 until his death in 1028. Born in the region of modern-day Vietnam, Lý Thái Tổ unified the local tribes and expanded his territory through strategic alliances and military campaigns. His reign marked the beginning of the Lý dynasty, which would go on to play a significant role in Vietnamese history. The capital city of Thăng Long was established during his rule, and it remained the imperial capital for over 800 years. Lý Thái Tổ's legacy extends beyond his military conquests, as he also promoted Buddhism and supported the arts. He is remembered as a wise and just ruler, who brought stability and prosperity to his people. The Lý dynasty's cultural achievements, including the development of the Vietnamese writing system, were heavily influenced by his patronage. In 2013, Lý Thái Tổ was posthumously awarded the title of 'Lý Thái Tổ' (Lý the Great Founder) by the Vietnamese government. He is considered one of the most important figures in Vietnamese history, and his legacy continues to be celebrated and studied by scholars today.
